newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity to hold NY investors meeting on Tueday.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity to hold NY investors meeting on Tueday.

text.p: Fidelity Investments, the closely held mutual fund giant, said it will hold meetings in New York on Tuesday with top institutional as well as retail clients about its fund performances and plans for 1997.

"It's an opportunity for us to have a dialogue with our customers," said a spokeswoman. "We know and understand Fidelity's investment performance and plans for the future have a significant impact on our customers."
Fidelity watchers said it will use the sessions to reassure investors it intends to slow turnover among portfolio managers and stick closer to stated investment goals.

Top Fidelity officials expected to attend include Paul Hondros, president of Fidelity Investments retail group; Gary Burkhead, president of Fidelity Mangement and Research Co (investment adviser arm) and president of Fidelity Investment Institutional Services, as well as several unnamed portfolio managers.
Private meetings with institutional clients will be held throughout the day at the Waldorf-Astoria hotel in mid-Manhattan.
Fidelity will meet in the hotel's grand balroom at 1830 EST/ 2330 GMT with individual retail clients and reporters.
Fidelity is holding meetings around the United States after being hit with declining market share, defections from its ranks of fund managers, and poor returns over the last year.
Another session was set for January 30 in Boston.
